haiku-low.q1: Returns 202 with its rejection list (position and reason) only after every valid event's append is acknowledged by all replicas.
haiku-low.q2: On a 5xx it resends the same batch. A timeout is only covered when the collector returns 5xx. The response to 429 is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q3: The copy appended first wins. Later copies are dropped while the 8-day dedup key lasts; longer gaps are NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q4: Tuesday's partition and replay. Day is the UTC day of the server-stamped received_at, not the client timestamp.
haiku-low.q5: In the existing KV store, keyed by event_id with value (partition, offset, received_at). Per-key 8-day TTL expiry removes entries.
haiku-low.q7: Micro-batch IDs derive from partition and offset range, and loads are idempotent per ID, so retries never double-insert. KV accepts same-offset reprocessing.
haiku-low.q8: Input is the archive only: day D plus event_ids from D-8 to D-1. Rebuilt events go to a staging table, then one atomic partition swap.
haiku-low.q9: It drops any day-D event_id seen in archive days D-8 to D-1, then keeps only the lowest (partition, offset) copy within day D.
haiku-low.q10: The live partition is unchanged, since nothing is visible before the atomic swap. The operator re-runs the replay safely.
haiku-low.q11: Only closed UTC days (after 02:00 UTC on D+1) within the archive window, roughly 82 days back at the oldest.
haiku-low.q12: Undecided by product. Options are dropping after dedup, or keeping with a nullable is_bot flag at the no-op step.

sonnet.q1: It validates per event: rejects those missing event_id/device_id or over 32 KB, records each rejection with batch position and reason, and continues with valid ones. It returns 202 (with the rejection list) only after every valid event's append to the raw log is acknowledged by all replicas.
sonnet.q2: On 5xx or timeout, the client resends the same batch (already-appended events become duplicates, dropped later by dedup). Rejected events are never retried. The 429 case is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q3: The first copy appended to the raw log wins (same partition via hash(event_id)). Live, the KV key lasts 8 days, so a copy arriving later than that would not be recognized live; for replay, the earlier 8 days are checked. The document does not say explicitly what happens past the 8 days live; the winner is the first received copy.
sonnet.q4: Tuesday. The day is the UTC day of the server-stamped received_at (00:10 Tuesday); the client timestamp is never used for partitioning or replay.
sonnet.q5: In the existing KV store, keyed by event_id, with value (partition, offset, received_at), set via atomic set-if-absent. Entries are removed by a per-key TTL of 8 days.
sonnet.q7: Two mechanisms: micro-batches have a deterministic ID from partition and offset range, and the loader is idempotent per micro-batch ID (or a load-ledger table), so a retried batch never inserts twice. Dedup treats a key with the same (partition, offset) as a reprocess and a first copy again, so the winner is not dropped. The log/archive retains the events, so nothing is lost.
sonnet.q8: It reads only the archive (day D plus event_ids from D-8 to D-1). Rebuilt events are written to a staging table (e.g. events_clean_staging_D_<runid>), not the live partition, until an atomic swap.
sonnet.q9: In the job's own memory or temp storage: it reads event_ids from archive days D-8 to D-1 as the earlier-won set. For each event_id in day D, it keeps a copy only if the id is not in the earlier-days set and the copy has the lowest offset among its copies in D (ordered by (partition, offset)); repeated (partition, offset) records are ignored.
sonnet.q10: The warehouse is unchanged: the replay writes only to staging, and nothing is visible until the single atomic swap. Dashboards keep seeing the old complete day. Recovery is to re-run the replay, which is safe.
sonnet.q11: Only closed days (now at or after 02:00 UTC on D+1) that are within the archive window, needing D plus 8 prior days, so the oldest replayable is about 82 days back. Also no other replay of D running, and all log-partition watermarks past 00:00 UTC on D+1.
sonnet.q12: Not decided (open decision: drop or keep with an is_bot flag). For now only a no-op placeholder step exists after dedup; no bot column or drop rule is added. The archive keeps raw events so a later decision can be applied via replay.
